displayPattern: Washer display shows 3C (also shown as 3E, E3 or 1 3C on some models)
meaning: Motor error: Samsung lists 3C, 3E, E3 and 1 3C as a motor error. On some models 3E is a voltage error instead, so check your user manual.
causes: A motor error detected by the washer, the meaning Samsung gives
diySteps: Power off the washer for 2-3 minutes
If the error continues, request service through Samsung's Support Center
safetyNote: Unplug the washer (or switch off its breaker) and close the water taps before you reach behind it, handle hoses or open a filter. Water left from a recent hot cycle can be very hot, so let it cool first. Never bypass the door lock. Motor, pump, valve, sensor and control-board repairs belong to a qualified appliance technician.
proAdvice: Samsung gives 3C no specific troubleshooting beyond the power cycle and restart; if it keeps returning, request service. Samsung's Smart Install self-test shows 3C when its high-speed spin check fails, but Samsung says not to run Smart Install while the washer is already showing an error code. If your manual lists 3E as a voltage error, use the 9C1 voltage-error page instead.
